claims.text: The nominal FeCoNiTi alloy was synthesized by rapid quenching.
The FeCoNiTi alloy has an fcc matrix containing hexagonal C14 Laves-phase precipitates.
C14 precipitates create phase boundaries that facilitate antiferromagnetic coupling between fcc Fe, Co, and Ni sublattices and the Ti-rich C14 phase.
The system exhibits ferromagnetic ordering transitions near 1084 K, 214 K, and 168 K.
Ti atoms mediate antiferromagnetic exchange coupling across fcc/C14 interfaces.
Interfacial antiferromagnetic coupling modifies the local electronic structure and spin density of states.
Antiferromagnetic coupling to the C14 phase suppresses the orbital moment of the fcc phase.
Suppression of the fcc orbital moment reduces saturation magnetization.
The C14 phase has high magnetocrystalline anisotropy relative to the fcc matrix.
Structural mismatch and magnetic anisotropy at the C14 phase provide strong domain-wall pinning sites.
Domain-wall pinning by the C14 phase increases coercivity.
The dual-phase alloy has a coercivity of approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
The dual-phase alloy has lower saturation magnetization than single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys have coercivity capped at 100 Oe because of insufficient orbital moments.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys lack effective domain-wall pinning mechanisms.
The proposed mechanism requires enough C14 phase to create continuous phase boundaries but not enough to dominate the magnetic response.
The coercivity-enhancement mechanism performs optimally around 400 K.
Spin-polarized DFT should be used to calculate phase- and element-resolved spin density of states at the Fermi level and orbital moments for fcc and C14 FeCoNiTi.
Magnetization and coercivity should be compared among single-phase fcc FeCoNiTi, dual-phase material, and C14-dominant FeCoNiTi to isolate phase-specific behavior.
Failure to detect C14-induced antiferromagnetic coupling or suppression of the fcc orbital moment would falsify the hypothesis.
